description: Speed the two-level path per-block orthonormalization on shape 9 (clustered512, now ~39ms). brief-64 nsys shows shape-9 is dominated by an FP64 CholeskyQR (d884gemm ~34 percent + 18.7 percent) that _eigh_twolevel keeps for the cond~1e6 ill-conditioned blocks. Route the well-conditioned blocks (most of the batch) off FP64 onto FP32-accurate 3xTF32 CholeskyQR2, keeping FP64 only for the genuinely ill-conditioned blocks detected by a cheap per-block conditioning probe (diag of the Gram / cheap norm ratio). Per-matrix residual-gated, cuSOLVER fallback. Pure torch.

t1: two-level orthonormalization FP64 per-block CQR -> 3xTF32 per-block CQR2 + 2x P+/P- spectral-projection re-purification (kills cross-block leakage fp32 R^-1 amplifies; joint CQR mixes +-1 cols -> eigen-gate fails, so orthonormalization must stay per-block for the block-L trick). 0 fallback, orth_max 0.003x gate, but shape 9 39538->88368us (too many GEMMs).

t2: cut reprojection 2->1. FINDING: per-block 3xTF32 CQR breaks cross-block orth for ALL blocks (cond<1e3 -> leak 0.26 min 0.079 ~17x gate; grows with cond), NOT just the ill-conditioned tail -- the brief's well-conditioned-majority premise is false here. Cross-block decoupling via reprojection restores it but adds ~a second set of projector A@Q GEMMs. shape 9 70731us, 0 fallback (seed 770004), geomean 30594. Regression: reprojection A@Q + fp32 trsm (18.4pct, 36 inst) exceed parent FP64 CQR.

t3: per-pass Gram precision (CQR2 pass1 3xTF32, pass2+reproj-reCQR plain TF32) + reprojection-precision knob. Cutting Ozaki bmms did NOT help: plain torch.bmm TF32 picks the same slow Ampere s1688gemm on batched tall-skinny blocks. shape 9 78250us (~t2), geomean 30881. The reprojection A@Q cost is the wall, not Gram bmm count.

t4: restore all-3x per-block CQR2 + reproj re-CQR (best config). Profile shape 9: FP64 CQR d884gemm ELIMINATED (was ~26pct of the ~41pct total d884gemm) -> only the initial FP64 projectors remain as d884gemm (16.3pct). New cost: 3xTF32 Ozaki s1688gemm ~33pct + fp32 trsm 17.6pct + Ozaki/reproject adds 7.3pct. Net shape 9 39538->70884us (regression). 5-seed reseed sweep shapes 9/6/11: 0 cuSOLVER fallback, 0-4/1280 FP64 rescue, orth_max 0.17-0.56x gate. geomean 30638. Other shapes unchanged. 39/39, stream absent. FINDING: the CQR moves off FP64 cleanly but the cross-block reprojection needed to keep the projector-split orthogonality (per-block 3xTF32 breaks it for ALL blocks) costs more than the FP64 CQR it replaces.

Brief-66 (two-level shape-9 orthonormalization FP64->3xTF32): 4 trials, HEAD 6556d0f8, geomean 30638us (parent 29175), shape 9 70884us (parent 39538) -- a REGRESSION, but the CQR d884gemm IS eliminated. KEY MEASURED FINDING (the brief's premise tested and refuted for this problem): per-block 3xTF32 CholeskyQR breaks the CROSS-block orthogonality Qp^T Qm for ESSENTIALLY ALL blocks, not just an ill-conditioned tail -- bucketed on shape 9, even cond<1e3 blocks leak 0.26 (min 0.079, ~17x the gate); it grows with cond but is high everywhere. So there is no 'well-conditioned majority' plain 3xTF32 CQR handles gate-cleanly; the fp32 Gram error (6e-6) amplified by even mild cond~1e3 through R^-1 leaks ~0.25 into the opposite eigenspace, which the two-level path relied on the FP64 projector to keep at ~1e-8. A JOINT 3xTF32 CQR fixes orth (~1e-5) but its upper-tri R^-1 MIXES +-1 columns -> the cheap block-L=+-1 assignment breaks and the eigen-residual gate mass-fails (eigr/|A| ~0.09 >> 9.2e-3). Block Gram-Schmidt fails too (not eigenvector-purifying). The ONLY working fix is a spectral-projection re-purification P+ Qp=(A Qp+Qp)/2 / P- Qm (uses A, so eigenvector-purifying): restores BOTH cross-block orth AND column purity -> 5-seed reseed sweep on shapes 9/6/11 gives 0 cuSOLVER fallback + 0-4/1280 FP64 rescue, orth_max 0.17-0.56x gate, 39/39, stream absent. BUT the reprojection A@Q (3xTF32 Ozaki, 3 bmms + adds) costs ~a second set of projectors, and the shape-9 profile shifts to s1688gemm 33pct + fp32 trsm 17.6pct + Ozaki adds 7.3pct, exceeding the parent's minimal FP64 CQR. FP64 d884gemm dropped 41pct->16.3pct (now only the untouched initial projectors). DONE: CQR2 pass counts, reprojection count 1/2, reprojection precision FP64/3xTF32 (FP64 ~4ms slower, B200 FP64 weak), per-pass Gram precision (plain-TF32 pass2 tripped rescue on ~all blocks -> reverted). OPEN DIRECTIONS I did NOT fully close: (1) cut the fp32 trsm (27 inst, 17.6pct) by replacing later CQR passes with Newton-Schulz (pure GEMM, no trsm) -- NS diverged after reprojection (leakage ~0.4 too large) but a NS pass-2 of the INITIAL CQR (well-conditioned) is untested; (2) the initial FP64 projectors (16.3pct) are now the largest FP64 block and were out of scope -- moving them to 3xTF32 would shrink d884gemm to ~0 but risks the raw ±1 separation; (3) whether a cheaper single fused A@Q reprojection (one n x n GEMM feeding both P+ and P- via slicing) + reusing that same A@Q for an eigen-residual check changes the economics. My strong measured read: moving JUST the two-level CQR off FP64 does not pay off because the cross-block coupling forces an extra A-projection whose cost >= the FP64 CQR saved; the lever with headroom is the initial FP64 projectors, not the CQR. Recommend rotating me or repointing at the projectors.
